audit.whatIsWrong: win[] and phases[].side gave Gwen levels 2, 3 and first item, contradicting whys[1], whys[2] and whys[5].
audit.why: His Body Slam stun plus W sustain out-stat Gwen at 2; the Q+E trade window at 3 and the Riftmaker timing are both described as evening out, not winning. Only the two-item 1v1 is stated as Gwen's.
audit.corrected: Skill / Gragas / Skill / Gragas / Gragas / Skill / Gwen.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Bait his E first' and 'hold your own R to re-engage after his knockback' with no cooldowns on either ability.
audit.why: Body Slam is 14/13.5/13/12.5/12 and Explosive Cask 100/85/70, against Hallowed Mist at 22s and Needlework at 120s. His engage returns faster than your mist does, and his ult returns faster than your ult - both of those change what 'bait it and punish' actually means here.
audit.corrected: early, mid and spikes[1].text now carry the numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Happy Hour's healing and Drunken Rage's auto-attack reset are both absent.
audit.why: Happy Hour carries the heal flag and restores health on every ability cast, so his barrel poke is also his sustain - that is why the page's 'trade for tempo, not a kill' instinct is right but under-explained. Drunken Rage carries autoReset, so the empowered hit lands on the swing wind-up, which is the moment Hallowed Mist has to already be down.
audit.corrected: early and wants.foe[1] now name Happy Hour's per-cast healing and the Grievous Wounds answer; mid names the Drunken Rage reset.

audit.why: Happy Hour heals per cast and Drunken Rage adds damage reduction on top, so the extended mist duel the page tells you to force is the fight Grievous Wounds decides.
audit.corrected: late and whys[6] now name it.

edits.before: Levels 1-3 are a careful AP brawl — neither of you wants to over-commit. Gragas can poke with his barrel and heal off Drunken Rage W, so don't walk up for a clunky cone Q he can just sustain back. By level 2-3, once you have Q+E, you can Skip 'n Slash in, land the center-snip true damage, and dash back out before his Body Slam E is up to stun you. Respect his W sustain: it lets him out-heal chip damage, so trade for tempo and farm, not for a kill you can't close.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 are a careful AP brawl — neither of you wants to over-commit. Gragas pokes with the barrel and Happy Hour heals him on every cast, so do not walk up for a clunky cone Q he simply sustains back. By 2-3, once you have Q+E, you can Skip 'n Slash in, land the centre-snip true damage, and dash back out inside his 14s Body Slam cooldown. Respect that per-cast healing: it out-paces chip, so trade for tempo and farm rather than a kill you cannot close, and plan Grievous Wounds into your build.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 belong to Gragas — his Explosive Cask R is the problem. He can Body Slam E onto you and ult-knockback to shove you clean OUT of your Hallowed Mist, stripping your untargetability mid-fight, or fling you off a target you were chaining needles into. Don't drop W early and stand in it like a safe zone; he'll just E-R you off it. Bait his E first, mist as it lands so the slam's stun whiffs, then snip. Hold your own R to re-engage after his knockback, not before.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 belong to Gragas — Explosive Cask is the problem. He Body Slams onto you and ult-knockbacks to shove you clean OUT of your Hallowed Mist, stripping the untargetability, or flings you off a needle target. Do not drop W early and stand in it like a safe zone. Bait the 14s Body Slam, mist as it lands so the stun whiffs, then snip — and watch the swing wind-up, because Drunken Rage is an auto reset. His R is 100s against your 120s, so hold Needlework for after the knockback.

edits.before: Once Riftmaker comes online the lane flips even and the late game is yours. A scaling AP brawler like Gragas has a fat HP bar and no real escape past one telegraphed Body Slam — exactly what your %-max-HP Snip Snip! and Thousand Cuts healing want to grind on. His Drunken Rage W damage reduction and sustain only delay it. Drag him into your Hallowed Mist for extended duels and out-sustain him. His one out is roaming off that R displacement, so keep him pinned: in a straight 1v1 at two items, you win.
edits.after: Once Riftmaker comes online the lane flips even and the late game is yours. A scaling AP brawler like Gragas has a fat HP bar and no real escape past one telegraphed Body Slam — exactly what %-max-HP Snip Snip! and A Thousand Cuts healing want to grind on. His Drunken Rage reduction and Happy Hour sustain only delay it, and Grievous Wounds removes the delay. Drag him into Hallowed Mist for extended duels and out-sustain him. His one out is roaming off the R displacement, so keep him pinned: in a straight 1v1 at two items, you win.

edits.before: You out-scale him 1v1 — magic %-HP shred plus passive healing beat a no-escape AP brawler the longer the fight goes.
edits.after: You out-scale him 1v1 — %-HP shred, passive healing and Grievous Wounds beat a no-escape brawler the longer it goes.

edits.before: Gragas spikes hardest here: his Explosive Cask R can knock you OUT of your Hallowed Mist, stripping the untargetability mid-fight, or flip the displacement to peel and roam — any fight he starts at 6 is his.
edits.after: Gragas spikes hardest here: a 100s Explosive Cask can knock you OUT of your Hallowed Mist, stripping the untargetability mid-fight, or flip the displacement to peel and roam — any fight he starts at 6 is his.

edits.before: Riftmaker/Nashor's online — %-max-HP Snip Snip! plus Thousand Cuts healing lets you out-grind his Drunken Rage W sustain-and-damage-reduction brawls and even the lane.
edits.after: Riftmaker/Nashor's online — %-max-HP Snip Snip! plus A Thousand Cuts healing and Grievous Wounds out-grind his Drunken Rage reduction and Happy Hour sustain, evening the lane.

edits.after: Reach Riftmaker and Grievous Wounds, then grind his HP bar with %-max-HP Snip Snip! and passive healing

notes: Ability names correct, prose second-person, and the key interaction (Explosive Cask knocking you out of your own Hallowed Mist) is already there and is genuinely good. Fixes: (1) the chart gave Gwen levels 2, 3, first item and two items while the whys give Gragas 2, call 3 and first item even, and only give Gwen two items - corrected to Skill/Gragas/Skill/Gragas/Gragas/Skill/Gwen. (2) No cooldowns: Body Slam is 14s at rank 1 and Explosive Cask 100s, which is exactly the pair the page tells you to bait and then punish. (3) Happy Hour (P) heals him on every ability cast and is never mentioned, so no anti-heal is ever called on a champion who sustains through chip by design. (4) Drunken Rage (W) is an auto-attack reset, so the empowered swing arrives on the attack wind-up rather than the cast - the page treats W purely as sustain. 'Thousand Cuts' was missing its 'A' in four places.
